name: People killed in traffic crashes (FARS)
plain: How many people died in traffic crashes in the municipio each year.
definition: People who died within 30 days of a crash on a public road in the municipio, as NHTSA's Fatality Analysis Reporting System counts them.

coverage.frequency: One year at a time; 2024 is NHTSA's first release (Annual Report File) and can change with the final file (refresh unit crashes)

method: crashes.py reads the Puerto Rico FARS files of each year: accident.csv for each fatal crash and its municipio (COUNTY, a county code; 72 means not given, counted in Puerto Rico's total only), person.csv for each person killed (INJ_SEV 4) and who they were (PER_TYP 5 pedestrian, 6 and 7 cyclists; drivers and passengers of a BODY_TYP 80-89 vehicle are motorcyclists). Checks that stop the build: every county code is a municipio or 72; the municipios and the crashes not placed add up to Puerto Rico's total each year.
source_detail: NHTSA FARS, Puerto Rico files 2020-2024 (https://static.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa/downloads/FARS/<year>/Puerto Rico/FARS<year>PuertoRicoCSV.zip): accident.csv (COUNTY, FATALS), person.csv (INJ_SEV, PER_TYP, BODY_TYP).
how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 288 deaths in 2024 (242 in 2020). Most in 2024: San Juan (35), Bayamón (16), Carolina (11).
caveats: Counts only: the observatory never publishes a crash's place, date or time.
2024 is NHTSA's first release and can change when the final file comes out.
A municipio has few deaths a year, so a year-to-year change can be chance; the five-year rates are steadier.
FARS can differ from the Puerto Rico Traffic Safety Commission's own count.

name: Traffic deaths per 100,000 residents, 2020-2024 (FARS)
plain: How many people died in traffic crashes in the municipio each year for every 100,000 residents, averaged over 2020-2024.
definition: The people killed in traffic crashes in the municipio over 2020-2024, divided by the sum of its residents in those years (Census Bureau population estimates), times 100,000: a yearly rate. Five years are pooled because a municipio has few deaths a year.
method: crashes.py reads the Puerto Rico FARS files of each year: accident.csv for each fatal crash and its municipio (COUNTY, a county code; 72 means not given, counted in Puerto Rico's total only), person.csv for each person killed (INJ_SEV 4) and who they were (PER_TYP 5 pedestrian, 6 and 7 cyclists; drivers and passengers of a BODY_TYP 80-89 vehicle are motorcyclists). Checks that stop the build: every county code is a municipio or 72; the municipios and the crashes not placed add up to Puerto Rico's total each year.
source_detail: NHTSA FARS, Puerto Rico files 2020-2024 (https://static.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa/downloads/FARS/<year>/Puerto Rico/FARS<year>PuertoRicoCSV.zip): accident.csv (COUNTY, FATALS), person.csv (INJ_SEV, PER_TYP, BODY_TYP).
how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 8.9 per 100,000 a year over 2020-2024. Highest: Santa Isabel (22.1), Guánica (21.7), Salinas (21.5); lowest: Culebra (0.0), Guayanilla (2.3), Las Marías (2.3).
caveats: Counts only: the observatory never publishes a crash's place, date or time.
2024 is NHTSA's first release and can change when the final file comes out.
A municipio has few deaths a year, so a year-to-year change can be chance; the five-year rates are steadier.
FARS can differ from the Puerto Rico Traffic Safety Commission's own count.
It counts the deaths on the municipio's roads, also of people who live elsewhere: high where much traffic passes through (see the rate per vehicle-km).

name: Traffic deaths per 100 million vehicle-km, 2020-2024 (FARS, HPMS)
plain: How many people died in traffic crashes for every 100 million kilometers driven on the municipio's roads, over 2020-2024: the risk per kilometer driven.
definition: The people killed in traffic crashes in the municipio over 2020-2024, divided by the vehicle-kilometers driven on its roads in those years, times 100 million. The vehicle-kilometers are those of HPMS data year 2025 (traffic_series.json), counted for each of the 5 years: a measure of risk per kilometer driven, where the rate per resident is high because much traffic passes through.
method: crashes.py reads the Puerto Rico FARS files of each year: accident.csv for each fatal crash and its municipio (COUNTY, a county code; 72 means not given, counted in Puerto Rico's total only), person.csv for each person killed (INJ_SEV 4) and who they were (PER_TYP 5 pedestrian, 6 and 7 cyclists; drivers and passengers of a BODY_TYP 80-89 vehicle are motorcyclists). Checks that stop the build: every county code is a municipio or 72; the municipios and the crashes not placed add up to Puerto Rico's total each year.
source_detail: NHTSA FARS, Puerto Rico files 2020-2024 (https://static.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa/downloads/FARS/<year>/Puerto Rico/FARS<year>PuertoRicoCSV.zip): accident.csv (COUNTY, FATALS), person.csv (INJ_SEV, PER_TYP, BODY_TYP).
how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 1.05 over 2020-2024 (about 1.69 per 100 million vehicle-miles). Highest: Rincón (2.34), Yabucoa (2.16), Loíza (2.13); lowest: Culebra (0.00), Guayanilla (0.20), Aibonito (0.33).
caveats: Counts only: the observatory never publishes a crash's place, date or time.
2024 is NHTSA's first release and can change when the final file comes out.
A municipio has few deaths a year, so a year-to-year change can be chance; the five-year rates are steadier.
FARS can differ from the Puerto Rico Traffic Safety Commission's own count.
The vehicle-kilometers are those of HPMS data year 2025, used for each of the five years; traffic changed over the period.
